title: Power Round — Spring 2021 — ARML Power sub-problem rubric

criteria.name: Problem 1
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1 (1 pt). Statement: 1. Given that the set of odd positive integers, {1, 3, 5, 7,...} is one set in a bipartition of the positive integers, determine its complement.

criteria.name: Problem 2
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2 (1 pt). Statement: 2. The set of prime positive numbers and the set of composite positive numbers taken together do not form a bipartition of the positive integers. Why not?

criteria.name: Problem 3a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3a (2 pts). Statement: 3. Let x = p q in lowest terms, so thatp andq are positive integers with no common factors. (a) Given that positive integer n is in X, show that n +p is also in X.

criteria.name: Problem 3b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3b (2 pts). Statement: (b) Given that positive integer m is in X′, show that m +p is also in X′.

criteria.name: Problem 4
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4 (2 pts). Statement: 4. If p> 2q then the least number inX is⌊p q⌋≥ 2 and the least number inX′ is clearly 1. On the other hand, if q < p <2q, show that the least positive integer in X′ is⌈ q p−q⌉.

criteria.name: Problem 5
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5 (2 pts). Statement: 5. Compute the ﬁrst ten terms of the Beatty sequence generated by φ = 1+ √ 5 2 ≈ 1.618.

criteria.name: Problem 6
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6 (2 pts). Statement: 6. Compute the ﬁrst ten terms of the Beatty sequence generated by φ2 = 3+ √ 5 2 ≈ 2.618.

criteria.name: Problem 7
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7 (1 pt). Statement: 7. Show that 1 φ + 1 φ2 = 1.

criteria.name: Problem 8
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8 (3 pts). Statement: 8. Let α andβ be any two irrational numbers greater than 1 such that 1 α + 1 β = 1. Prove that there are no positive integers m, i, and j such that m =⌊iα⌋ =⌊jβ⌋. That is, with the given restrictions on α and β, no number appears in both of their Beatty sequences.

criteria.name: Problem 9
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9 (3 pts). Statement: 9. Under the same conditions on α and β, as in the previous problem, prove that every positive integer appears in either the Beatty sequence generated by α or the Beatty sequence generated by β, or both.

criteria.name: Problem 10
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10 (2 pts). Statement: 10. Show that the Beatty sequence for an irrational number α >1 can never contain all the terms of any nonconstant arithmetic sequence.

criteria.name: Problem 11
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 11 (2 pts). Statement: 11. While the facts about complementary Beatty sequences are fascinating enough, show that the diﬀerence between the nth term of the sequence generated by φ2 and the nth term of the sequence generated by φ is exactly n.

criteria.name: Problem 12a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 12a (2 pts). Statement: 12. The complementarity doesn’t quite work for rational numbers. Let x = p q in lowest terms and y = p p−q so that x andy are both greater than 1 and 1 x + 1 y = 1. Prove that the sequences X ={⌊kx⌋}∞ k=1 and Y ={⌊ky⌋}∞ k=1 are not complementary by showing that: (a) X∩Y ={kp}∞ k=1, the sequence of positive multiples of p.

criteria.name: Problem 12b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 12b (2 pts). Statement: (b) X∪Y contains all positive integers excluding the sequence{kp− 1}∞ k=1.

criteria.name: Problem 13
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 13 (4 pts). Statement: 13. Prove that Yα is the Beatty sequence generated by 1 α.

criteria.name: Problem 14
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 14 (3 pts). Statement: 14. Let Q be any nondecreasing sequence of nonnegative integers, and let Q∗ be its fre- quency sequence. Prove that Q∗∗, the frequency sequence of the frequency sequence, is equal to the original sequence Q. That is, prove that Q =Q∗∗.

criteria.name: Problem 15
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 15 (2 pts). Statement: 15. Let Q be any nondecreasing sequence of nonnegative integers, Q ={q1,q 2,q 3,... }, and deﬁne the sequenceP ={q1 +1,q 2 +2,q 3 +3,...}. Prove that P is a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers.

criteria.name: Problem 16
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 16 (4 pts). Statement: 16. Let Q and P be as deﬁned in the previous problem, and let Q∗ be the frequency sequence of Q, given by Q∗ ={f1,f 2,f 3,...}. Deﬁne P∗ from Q∗ as in the previous problem: P∗ ={f1 + 1,f 2 + 2,f 3 + 3,...}. Prove that P∗ is, in fact, the complement P′.
